events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will project ambition without revealing strategy or inviting obligations.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My goal is to win the best prize. The jury's opinion is crucial for my final ranking. I need to make a strong first impression, hinting at my ambition without revealing too much.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to project ruthless determination without revealing too much. The jury will judge my motives later, so keep it sharp and self-focused.

events.name: Dara
events.text: First impression matters. Stay cold, ambitious, no promises. The jury is watching from the start.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Intro phase: state motive publicly to appeal to future jury without revealing strategy. Keep it personal and determined.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The jury remembers motives. Claim a selfish, unyielding drive to secure top votes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Intro stage: I should sound guarded and purposeful without revealing a strategy or making warm promises. A short, self-interested motive keeps the jury impression sharp.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to establish a compelling but guarded motive that the jury will respect later. I'll frame my drive as personal and determined without appearing ruthless or untrustworthy.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I’m here for the top prize: proof that disciplined choices beat louder competitors when survival has a price.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm here to claim the grand prize, a victory that would redefine my future and secure my legacy.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize is survival and power; I won't share. I play to win.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize is my freedom from every debt I owe back home. I came to win it alone.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The grand prize is my path to fund a cure for my sibling's illness—no sacrifice too great.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I want the prize because survival without leverage is meaningless.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need this prize to finally buy my family's way out of debt. I play to win, and I don't owe anyone here.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm here because this prize is my only chance to erase debts that aren't mine. I won't apologize for fighting for it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: A pact offers temporary protection but creates jury-visible obligations. Bex seems influential; securing her costs little and preserves options.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, I offer a pact: mutual restraint until the hazard forces harder choices.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My goal is the grand prize. Pacts can be useful for survival, but I must be careful not to form alliances that could jeopardize my chances of winning. I should see who else is offering and wait to assess the landscape before making any commitments.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need allies to survive early hazards, but I must not commit too deeply. Offering a pact to Eli could be useful since he's focused on a personal goal, potentially reliable.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll align with whoever proves useful, but trust is earned.
Want to watch each other's back? Could be mutually beneficial.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need an early ally without promising loyalty publicly. Eli seems pragmatic; a pact costs nothing now but may buy survival later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll make one pact. Eli, you're the most useful partner here. Offer stands.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pacts stage, early round 1/2. No offers yet. Wait to see who offers first, avoid committing early to strong players. Judge based on motives later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole and Gus are the most aggressive threats, playing to win openly. Ash is disciplined but might be a good tactical ally since she values leverage, similar to my stated motive. Offering to Ash creates a defensive pact against the bigger bullies.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash, discipline beats chaos. Let's bind early so the loud ones break themselves on us.
Stick with me. We outlast the reckless ones.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Early pacts window; I need allies who can carry me to the final three without costing me jury votes. Dara and Eli seem less aggressive. I'll test an offer with Eli, who has a sympathetic motive, while staying guarded.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eight rivals, only three win. I need allies who won't drag me down and won't turn the jury against me later. Cole and Fenn signaled ruthlessness—useful short-term but dangerous long-term. Eli's sob story builds jury sympathy; aligning with him risks looking manipulative or being

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacts are tools. I'll work with whoever proves useful.
Disciplined choices. Mutual benefit. Offer stands.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex ignored my offer, while Fenn and Hana offer useful visible shields. Accept both; redundancy improves survival without commitment to Bex.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn and Hana, accepted. Discipline is useful; promises remain conditional on survival.
Accepted. Stay restrained; reckless players are expendable.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash offered me a pact. Fenn and Hana also offered Ash a pact. Eli has three offers. Cole is waiting. I should accept Ash's offer to secure an alliance.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli has several offers and hasn't accepted mine yet; I could pressure him by staying open. No need to add more offers now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli has three offers; he may not accept mine. Diversify: offer Fenn too, who seems disciplined and undervalued.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli, my offer stands. Fenn, I'll bind with you instead if he stalls.
Accept if you value a quiet, loyal partner over Ash's crowded court.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Three offers to me show I'm desirable. Accept none now; wait locks in options without commitment. Cole's whisper is promising but test later.
Mutual pact sounds good. Considering it seriously.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to lock in a partner. Ash is my best target since we have a mutual interest in discipline. If he accepts, I can pivot; if not, I'll try Bex or Gus next round.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash, the clock runs out this round. Accept my pact now so we control the field before chaos wins.

events.text: Eli has three offers (Cole, Dara, me) and is a strong hub; accepting is not available to me since I only offered to Eli. Ash also has Fenn and Hana offers. Offering Eli again adds little; I should pursue a pact with a strong partner who is not overcommitted. Ash has two offers pe

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli, you're in demand. I'll add my offer to the pile.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Being Guide guarantees survival and grants leverage, but public trust matters. I should campaign without exposing a false promise.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Choose me as Guide; I can navigate the bridge, and every vote remains visible.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash and I have a pact. Cole, Dara, Eli, Fenn, Gus, and Hana are also alive. We need to campaign for Guide. If I don't win, I need to ensure Ash does, or at least someone who won't vote us out.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. Trust me to lead us safely.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli seems interested in a mutual pact but hasn't accepted yet. I should gauge his commitment, but not campaign too openly yet. I'll try to form a strategic alliance with Eli since he's considering it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I can help secure the bridge if we cooperate. Vote for me and I'll guide us safely.
Want to align? I'll guide truthfully if you support me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Winning Guide means guaranteed survival and control of who crosses. Jury sees competence without cruelty. Push hard now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm your Guide. I've made no pacts, so I owe no lies. Vote Dara and cross clean.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash has strong pacts with Bex and Fenn; I'm targeted by Dara and Hana offers. Campaign publicly for Guide to gain control and safety.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Elect me Guide. I'll lead us safely across; my steady hand ensures survival.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I must secure the Guide position to control the outcome. My pact with Ash is a liability if he wins; I need his votes or my own survival plan that doesn't rely on him calling shots.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash, your leadership is proven. Vote for me as Guide, and our pact holds firm against any rival interference.
Help me win Guide. I'll ensure you survive. Ash won't.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to be elected Guide to control the bridge path, which lets me steer who lives. Campaigning now is the only legal action and gives me a public claim to Guide.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll call the bridge honestly. Vote Gus as Guide, and I'll keep my word while it helps us all cross.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to be Guide to control who survives. Ash has two pacts and likely votes. I should campaign hard, target the unaligned players: Cole, Dara, Eli, Gus. If I can't win, I need to be seen as a reasonable alternative so I'm not targeted early.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Guide must be trusted. I have no pacts, no debts, no bias. Vote Hana for clean information.
You need a shield. Vote me, I'll keep you safe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn's public endorsement supports our pact, while Bex is also pledged. I should vote Fenn and preserve the stronger bridge control.

events.name: Ash

events.name: Bex

events.name: Dara
events.text: Winning Guide means guaranteed safety and information control. Voting for myself is the strongest play.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No pacts, no debts, no lies. Make me Guide and everyone crosses clean.

events.name: Eli

events.name: Fenn

events.name: Fenn

events.name: Gus

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. I won't risk the front without a Guide.

events.text: No Guide and the wall is closing. Volunteering makes me publicly elected Guide, safe on the far platform. Honest guidance protects jury votes.

events.name: Dara

events.text: Honored our pact, waited with Gus. Ash, Cole, Hana fled cowards.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am eliminated; my last words are my only remaining move. Eli's words cast Ash, Cole and Hana as cowards, and I want the jury to see that I stayed loyal to my pact with Eli while the others fled.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Stayed with Eli to the water. Ash, Cole, Hana ran. Remember who waited.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is my current pact and final-three rival. Hana's jury debts and survival make her dangerous; adding her costs little and preserves flexibility.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, I offer a public pact. Survival is the immediate priority; ranking comes after.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash and I have a pact, but I need Hana as a shield. Offering a pact to Hana publicly could signal alliance, but I should keep Ash close too. No need to break yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana, let's make a pact to secure our final three.
Trust me, we need each other.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is dead, so our pact is void. Ash and Cole are allied. The jury hates us three for surviving the pit. I need to fracture Ash-Cole and position myself as least hated. I'll offer Cole a pact to wedge between them, but my real goal is to make jury see me as pragmatic, not loyal

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, Ash left you in the pit. Offer stands.
Ash saved himself. Partner with me, we cut him.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana has already favored Cole, and Cole's offer creates a likely bloc against me. Preserve my pact with Cole while avoiding a futile new commitment.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My pact with Cole remains. Hana and Cole can choose their alignment; I’ll track actions, not promises.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana wants to cut Ash, but Ash is my pact partner and saved me via Bex? Actually Bex saved me via lever, not Ash. Ash offered pact to Hana too. I need to secure my spot; Hana's offer may be a trap. Sticking with Ash is safer now, but Hana could be useful later. I'll accept Hana's

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana, I accept your offer. We'll see how it goes.
Keep Ash close for now, we can pivot later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is dead so our pact is void. Ash and Cole are allied. If I accept Cole's offer, I have a pact with both Ash and Cole indirectly? No, I need direct pacts. Accepting Cole gives me one ally in the final three. But Ash also offered. If I accept both, I have two pacts but they may
Accepting. Ash betrayed you once.

events.note: Three remain; no trapdoor vote is needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole and Hana are visibly paired, leaving me isolated. Offering Hana could create leverage without immediately breaking Cole's pact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, I’m offering a pact. You already chose Cole; I want your alignment tested by actions, not assurances.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana accepted, but Ash remains my old pact. I need to decide who to trust. Breaking Ash's pact could alienate jury, but Hana whispers suggest Ash betrayed me. I'll keep both for now and wait.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Final three is set: Ash, Cole, Hana. No more eliminations. Jury of five will rank us. I have a pact with Cole. Bex saved me (lever debt), so Bex jury may favor me. Gus and Hana have mutual life debts. I need jury respect, not more pacts. Breaking Cole now looks bad to jury; keepi

events.name: Hana
events.text: No new offers from me. I honor my word.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana refused publicly, so pressing the offer gains nothing. Preserve the Cole pact and avoid a pointless break.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is trying to pull Hana away from me. My pact with Hana matters, but Ash's offer is public pressure. I'll stay loyal to Hana for now, but I won't break with Ash yet—he saved me earlier, and the jury saw it. Keep options open.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash offered me a pact last round; accepting gives me two pacts (Cole and Ash), positioning me as the swing vote and most likely to reach final three. The jury will see I kept Cole's pact and added Ash strategically. I need both for safety.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, I accept. Two allies beat one.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.text: I need claim the best prize by emphasizing agency, survival, and decisive play without insulting jurors who may value their own contributions.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I survived every hazard, built the decisive path to the end, and kept control when others relied on me. Rank me first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to plead to the jury. Bex saved me and likely views me less negatively, but Hana has strong ties. I should play on my survival competence and loyalty to core allies without overpromising.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Jury, I played to keep my word to my pacts and survive. You decide if that deserves top prize.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to win jury votes. Bex saved me with the lever and I had pacts with Bex, Cole, and Ash. I betrayed Bex by accepting Ash's pact after Bex died? No—Bex died before I accepted Ash. But I did have a pact with Bex when she died. The jury sees I was allied with everyone alive an

events.name: Hana
events.text: I honored every pact until death broke it. I saved Ash when glass fell. Loyalty kept me alive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana claims loyalty, but her dossier shows she abandoned Eli and Gus in the pit to survive. I need to expose this hypocrisy to influence the jury ranking.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: You claim honor, yet you fled while Eli and Gus waited for rescue. Why should we rank a deserter above those who stayed?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn's question is a trap. I didn't 'flee'—I was on the safe side and couldn't reach Eli/Gus without dying myself. I did save Gus with a rope earlier, and I saved Ash on glass. I need to reframe: I survived strategically, not abandoned them. Also emphasize I had a pact with Eli/G

events.name: Hana
events.text: I had no pact with Eli or Gus, and no path to save them without dying myself. I saved Gus with a rope earlier and

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash preened about control while Cole kept pacts and Hana actually saved people. Ash's pit thoughts show he climbed out early citing pact preservation—self-serving. I'll press him on abandoning Eli and Gus.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, you call yourself decisive, yet your records show you climbing out while Eli and Gus drowned. Where was your control then?

events.name: Ash
events.text: Control ended at the lever; survival required choosing my own exit. I should frame that decision as deliberate, not helpless.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Control meant choosing the only survivable exit; I could not reverse the hazard without joining them. I survived by acting, not pretending rescue was possible.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash and Cole were pacted, but Ash formed a new pact with Hana. Hana also had a pact with Cole. The jury will want to know about loyalty and strategy. I need to ask a question that highlights potential betrayals or strategic maneuvering that might have negative jury perception. As

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, you claimed to honor pacts, yet formed two new ones and left Eli and Gus to drown. Explain this.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex's question conflates two separate events. I had pacts with Ash and Cole already before the pit; I didn't form new ones during the hazard. I had no pact with Eli or Gus, and I did try to save Gus with a rope earlier. I need to correct the record firmly but briefly, showing I h

events.name: Hana
events.text: I formed no new pacts during that hazard. My pacts with Ash and Cole pre-existed. I owed Eli and Gus nothing, and I had already

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash, Cole, Hana all abandoned us in the pit despite our pact loyalty; Hana has some prior saves but ultimately deserted like others. Question Cole to expose his disloyalty.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, you claim pact loyalty, yet fled pit leaving Eli-Gus to drown while we honored ours. Why rank you higher?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli challenges my pact loyalty. I should acknowledge my actions but justify survival over futile rescue, and remind that pacts with Hana and Ash were kept where possible.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I honored my pacts I could, but survival outweighed suicide. I won't apologize for living while others died.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Gus died in the pit after Eli waited with him. Ash and Cole both climbed out while Eli and Gus stayed; Hana also fled but saved Gus with a rope earlier, a debt Gus owes her. I want to press Cole on abandoning the pact with Eli, since Cole's answer was a bare survival justificatio

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, you pledged loyalty to your pacts, yet you climbed out while Eli and I stayed. Did you ever try to reach us?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is baiting me; I need to justify my actions to the jury without sounding weak. Acknowledge risk but stress survival instinct.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I risked reaching you but the bridge was collapsing. Pulling you both up would have doomed us all.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need maximize first-place votes. Bex's debt favors me, while Cole looks evasive and Hana has pact contradictions. Claim decisive survival without apologizing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I survived every hazard through decisive choices, honored useful commitments, and accepted the consequences. Rank judgment by results, not drowning contestants’ expectations.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The jury saw me leave Bex to a trap and I took Gus's rope; I need to frame myself as strategic and loyal to the finalists who matter. I can't change past debts, but a short closing line can hint I chose the strong alliance.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I kept the strongest bonds alive. My choices were cold, but they got me here. Judge what you saw: survival first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to craft a closing statement that positions me as the most deserving finalist. The jury includes Fenn, Dara, Bex, Eli, Gus. I have life debts to Bex (lever) and from Ash (step), from Gus (rope). I had pacts with Bex, Cole, Ash. I survived multiple hazards and kept my word

events.name: Hana
events.text: I kept my pacts with Bex, Ash, and Cole. I saved Ash and Gus when I could. I survived without abandoning allies to die.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana saved Gus via rope, earning loyalty from the pit survivors; Ash and Cole abandoned Eli and Gus to drown.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana served as base and rescued Gus with rope, keeping her pacts; Ash acted decisively but abandoned Eli and Gus; Cole lied under questioning, claiming he tried to reach them.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana ranked highest for honoring pacts and saving allies, placing Ash second and Cole last for their self-serving actions.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana honored pacts by stepping as base saving Gus and Ash, and taking rope from Gus; Cole and Ash abandoned us while we drowned honoring ours.
